subject: Follow-up: territorial data anchoring questions & next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: territorial data anchoring questions & next steps

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a short list of clarifying items so we can size options and get you a proposal: 

Recap:
- Primary ask: ensure patient PII and derived model artifacts remain under EU control for production inference.
- Desired DR posture: warm-standby in a second region (for availability) but no unrestricted cross-border retention of raw records.
- Compliance constraints: 7 year retention for patient records, audit log export to hospital SIEM permitted if logs remain in EU; legal team to confirm any exceptions.

Clarifying questions (please confirm / provide details):
1) Data locality: must all persistent PII (raw input and training traces) be restricted to EU region, or is de-identified derivative material allowed to leave the EU?
2) Backups: can encrypted backups be geo-replicated outside EU if keys remain in EU KMS, or is any cross-border replication disallowed?
3) Failover: acceptable RTO/RPO target for production (example: RTO < 15 min, RPO < 15 min)? Any hard SLAs required for failover activation?
4) Logs & monitoring: do you require audit logs to be retained longer than standard 90 days? If you want exports to an external SIEM, does that SIEM need to be hosted in the EU?
5) Data preservation: are there any legal holds or e-discovery rules we should account for beyond the 7-year retention?

Next steps I propose from Redwood:
- Marcus will document the default EU-anchored deployment pattern and options that meet your constraints (warm-standby, geo-backed encrypted backups, KMS placement).
- We’ll attach our SOC2 Type II and a short architecture sketch for reference.
- If answers above are quick, we’ll return a scoped technical proposal + rough cost estimate by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: SOC2 Type II (we'll attach), short architecture PDF.

Thanks — want to confirm the best technical contact for a deep-dive? (Is Luca the right person?)

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0126

From: Emma Watson <emma@zenwellhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: territorial data anchoring questions & next steps

Thanks Irene — helpful summary. Quick answers from our side so you can scope: 

- Data locality: patient-identifiable data (PII) and any records that can be re-linked MUST stay in the EU. De-identified embeddings/metrics that are provably non-reversible are OK to store or process outside EU but must be explicitly documented.
- Backups: we prefer that backups containing PII remain in EU. We can consider encrypted cross-border replication for non-PII artifacts if keys are managed by us and never leave EU.
- Failover: our ops team prefers RTO < 30 minutes and RPO < 5 minutes for critical inference endpoints. We may accept longer for non-critical batch jobs.
- Logs: retain audit logs 2 years, but security events must be retained 7 years. Any SIEM exports must be to an EU-hosted collector.
- Legal hold: possible ad hoc holds; we’ll flag those as needed but assume 7-year retention baseline.

Luca is the right technical lead — he’ll handle the deep dive. We also need an early ballpark price for the EU-pinned configuration + optional warm-standby in US. Can you include whether BYOK is required for us to allow any cross-border replication?

Thanks — attaching our data classification (csv) for context.

—Emma
Director, IT Security, ZenWell Health
emma@zenwellhealth.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Watson <emma@zenwellhealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-25T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: territorial data anchoring questions & next steps

Hi Emma — looping in technical details and options. Summary first, details below.

Short answer bullets:
- EU anchoring: Redwood can pin inference and primary persistent stores to an EU region (data at rest + KV caches).
- BYOK & KMS: To permit any cross-region replication of encrypted blobs, we require customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK) with key policies that allow rotation but not export. If keys cannot be exported out of EU, geo-replication can still occur if the ciphertext is moved and the KMS endpoint for decryption remains in EU via remote decrypt calls — this requires network arrangements and will increase failover latency/complexity.
- Backups: We support encrypted backups. Default behavior for EU-pinned customers is: backups containing PII remain stored in EU backups only. Optionally, customers may opt-in to replicate encrypted derivatives to a secondary region (e.g., warm-standby in US) provided BYOK or explicit legal authorization is in place.
- Failover posture: warm-standby (inactive replicas in another region with pre-warmed containers) is supported. Typical RTOs for that configuration are 5–20 minutes depending on session continuity needs; RPO down to 1–5 minutes if continuous KV replication is enabled (adds cost).
- Logs & SIEM: audit logs can be streamed to your EU SIEM via private peering (VPC peering/direct connect) or pushed over a TLS-forwarder. Retention windows are configurable per log type; default audit log retention is 90 days, security-event retention can be extended to 7 years on request.
- Model artifacts & caching: KV caches used for inference are ephemeral by default and do not persist raw inputs. If you require long-lived model traces to be retained, that is a separate option (we treat them as PII if linked to patient ids).

Operational considerations:
1) We recommend BYOK in the EU KMS for customers with strict geo controls — that gives you full control over key lifecycle and enables our legal team to authorize replication scenarios faster.
2) For legal holds, we can tag snapshots and prevent deletion while the hold is active; those snapshots will remain in the EU storage scope unless you explicitly allow cross-region movement.
3) Network design: to stream logs to a customer SIEM in EU, we’ll provision a dedicated egress with encryption-in-transit and log signing for tamper evidence.

Attached: SOC2 Type II (redwood) and a short architecture sketch that shows EU-anchored primary + optional warm-standby in US with encrypted replication lanes.

Next steps:
- We’ll produce two scoped options: (A) EU-only anchored production (no cross-border replication) with BYOK; (B) EU primary + warm-standby in US with encrypted geo-replication of non-PII derivatives and optional remote-decrypt for ciphertext that must remain EU-keyed. Expect the draft by tomorrow EOD.
- Pricing: we’ll include a delta line for continuous KV replication (RPO 1–5m) vs snapshot-based backup replication.

If you want, we can schedule a 60-minute tech deep dive with Luca + your network/security folks; Marcus and Monica will join. Proposed slots: Tue 27th 10–11am CET or Wed 28th 2–3pm CET.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
